chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who treats people with medicine and takes a fee for it; he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a doctor to charge money for treating patients in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on earnings, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) validates the professionalization of medicine by permitting physicians to charge a fee (ju'lan) for their services. This ruling distinguishes medical practice from gratuitous charity, acknowledging the physician's expertise and time as legitimate commodities for exchange, a principle foundational to Islamic medical jurisprudence.
